item.title: CDC chief quits: Susan Monarez resigns weeks into role; vaccine policy rift with Kennedy
item.description: Susan Monarez resigned as CDC director shortly after assuming the role, reportedly due to disagreements with Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. The clashes stemmed from Kennedy's decision to replace vaccine advisory panel members with vaccine guideline critics. Her departure follows CDC restructuring, budget cuts, and concerns over misinformation, particularly regarding vaccines, within the agency.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US visa shake-up: No more ‘duration of status’; plans fixed stay limits for foreign students, exchange visitors
item.description: The United States Department of Homeland Security plans to change visa rules. The new rules impact students, exchange visitors, and foreign media representatives. Currently, these visa holders can stay indefinitely. The proposed change sets a maximum four-year stay for students and exchange visitors. Media representatives get a 240-day limit. Officials say this will reduce fraud and improve oversight.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: IAEA back in Iran: First since US strikes on nuclear facilities; only limited access cooperation still uncertain
item.description: IAEA inspectors have resumed limited operations in Iran, visiting the Bushehr nuclear facility for the first time since cooperation was suspended in June following US strikes. While this marks a partial resumption, full access to all sites, including those targeted in the attacks, remains uncertain. Discussions continue amid warnings that further actions, like snapback sanctions, could halt IAEA engagement entirely.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Sub thrown, charges dropped: Prosecutors fail to indict ‘sandwich guy’ - questions over Trump’s law enforcement
item.description: A federal grand jury declined to indict Sean Charles Dunn, a former Justice Department employee, who was filmed throwing a sandwich at a CBP agent during a 2020 protest in Washington, D.C. Dunn was arrested on assault charges and subsequently fired after the incident, which occurred during heightened federal law enforcement activity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Putin’s next-gen military? Eight-year-old kids train with rifle & grenade; 'to serve my country and be loyal'
item.description: In Russia's Rostov region, near the Ukrainian border, children as young as eight are participating in combat-style exercises at a summer camp. The program, supervised by soldiers with Ukraine frontline experience, involves grenade throwing, rifle handling, and simulated combat. This initiative aims to instill military values and prepare youngsters for future service, reflecting President Putin's broader push for youth militarization.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Minneapolis church mass shooting: Trump orders flag at half mast; FBI begins terror, hate crime probe
item.description: Following a tragic mass shooting at a Minneapolis church on August 27, which claimed the lives of two students and injured 17 others, President Trump has ordered flags to be flown at half-staff. The FBI is investigating the incident, led by Director Kash Patel, as both an act of domestic terrorism and a hate crime targeting the Catholic community.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘It was my right as a citizen’: Flag-burning veteran challenges Trump order; says ‘will go to jail’
item.description: Jay Carey, a decorated US Army veteran, was arrested for burning an American flag near the White House as a protest against President Trump's executive order targeting flag desecration. Carey, who served in the Iraq War, claims his actions were protected under the First Amendment and intended to challenge perceived government overreach.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Abrego Garcia’s deportation paused: US judge delays removal to October; Trump officials to testify
item.description: A US federal judge has temporarily halted the deportation of Kilmar Abrego Garcia, previously deported under the Trump administration, scheduling an evidentiary hearing for October 6. Abrego Garcia, currently in ICE custody, faces potential deportation to Uganda, prompting a credible fear interview. He is also pursuing a renewed asylum claim, adding complexity to his legal battle against deportation.

item.title: Five episodes that soured the Trump-Modi bromance
item.description: The Trump-Modi friendship, once hailed as a 'bromance,' faced several challenges during Trump's presidency. Key disagreements arose from Trump's offer to mediate in Kashmir, misunderstandings during meetings, and trade disputes. Ultimately, the relationship soured due to perceived slights and conflicting priorities, culminating in Trump's rejection of a trade deal.

item.title: Insights from UK’s unlikely ‘Blue Zone’ where people regularly live past 100
item.description: Plymouth emerges as the UK's healthiest city for midlifers, mirroring global Blue Zones known for longevity. The Midlife Clarity Index highlights the impact of diet, exercise, and social connections on wellbeing. Emphasizing proactive health steps and regular assessments, the study suggests that adopting these lifestyle habits can significantly improve health outcomes and extend lifespan.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Shooting at Minneapolis Catholic school: At least 20 hurt as gunman opens fire; Donald Trump reacts
item.description: A shooting at Annunciation Church in Minneapolis resulted in two fatalities and at least 17 injuries. President Trump acknowledged the incident, offering prayers and confirming the FBI's rapid response. Authorities are investigating reports of a potential bomb within the church, while urging residents to avoid the area as emergency services assist victims and the shooter is contained.

item.title: Saudi Arabia introduces Tourism and Hospitality as core subject for grade 12 students
item.description: Saudi Arabia has introduced Tourism and Hospitality as a core subject for third-grade secondary students, alongside new electives like Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Fashion, and First Aid. Part of Vision 2030 reforms, the curriculum emphasizes practical skills, innovation, and sustainability. Developed with key ministries, the changes aim to modernize education, support economic diversification, and foster real-world readiness in students.

item.title: From tariffs to tuition: Donald Trump just welcomed 600,000 Chinese students and MAGA can't keep calm
item.description: While Trump’s constant delays has earned him the sobriquet TACO (Trump always chickens out), his latest move has made things even more difficult for the MAGA faithful to swallow: greenlighting the entry of 600,000 Chinese students.

item.title: 'Inevitable': Israel on Gaza City evacuation; remarks come as Trump prepares to host talks on post-war Palestine plans
item.description: An Israeli military spokesperson announced the "inevitable" evacuation of Gaza City amidst intensified operations against Hamas. The UN has warned of a potential famine due to this evacuation plan. Meanwhile, US President Trump plans to discuss post-war Gaza strategies.

item.title: Saudi Arabia and Syria sign historic $24 billion in investment deals across 12 sectors at first joint forum
item.description: Saudi Arabia and Syria held their first joint investment forum in Riyadh, marking a major step in renewing economic ties. The event saw 450 participants and resulted in $24 billion worth of investment agreements across 12 sectors. Officials highlighted growing trade, rising bilateral investments, and plans to support Syria’s reconstruction through long-term, structured economic cooperation.
